rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cloth story, Jesus produces garments in the requested colors; a disciple recognizes the miracle as from God, believes, and joins his companions as a disciple.
rows.anchor: فأخرج عيسى ثوبا أحمر وثوبا أصفر وثوبا أخضر إلى أن أخرجها على الألوان التي أرادها

rows.speaker: مصعب
rows.claim: Musʿab says Jesus had twelve disciples, who received miraculous bread and water; Jesus praised earning one's living by hand, so they washed clothes for wages.
rows.anchor: روى يوسف الفريابي عن مصعب قال: الحواريون إثنا عشر رجلا اتبعوا عيسى بن مريم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains that the disciples were called ḥawāriyyūn because their hearts were pure.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: سموا حواريين لصفاء قلوبهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak says they were called ḥawāriyyūn because they were luminous, bearing the trace, light, and beauty of worship; he links this to 48:29.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن المبارك: سموا حواريين لأنهم كانوا نورانيين عليهم أثر العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root ḥ-w-r denotes intense whiteness: aḥwar and ḥawrāʾ describe whiteness of the eye, ḥawārī fine white flour, and taḥwīr the act of whitening.
rows.anchor: وأصل الحور عند العرب شدة البياض

rows.speaker: ابن [حلزة]
rows.claim: Ibn Ḥalaza's verse uses ḥawāriyyāt for women, as evidence for the word's Arabic usage.
rows.anchor:
قال ابن [حلزة] :
فقل للحواريات يبكين غيرنا

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq's verse also uses ḥawāriyyāt in describing women beneath their veils.
rows.anchor:
وقال الفرزدق:
فقلت أن الحواريات تغطية

rows.speaker: ابن عون
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAwn recounts that a king's serving bowl never diminished while Jesus ate; the king followed Jesus, along with his people, and they became disciples.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عون: صنع ملك من الملوك طعاما.

rows.speaker: الكلبي وأبو روق
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Abu Rawq identify the ḥawāriyyūn as Jesus's chosen, intimate followers, numbering twelve men.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي وأبو روق: الحواريون أصفياء عيسى وكانوا إثنا عشر رجلا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the ḥawāriyyūn are the helpers, and a ḥawārī is a supporter.
rows.anchor: الحسن: الحواريون الأنصار والحواري الناصر

rows.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
rows.claim: Thaʿlabī cites ʿAmr ibn Kulthum's boast that his people answer provocation with even greater retaliation.
rows.anchor: وقال عمرو بن كلثوم: ألا لا يجهلن أحد علينا

rows.speaker: جنيد
rows.claim: Asked how God can approve for Himself the plotting He condemns in others, Junayd first says he does not know what the questioner means.
rows.anchor: سأل رجل جنيدا كيف رضي المكر لنفسه، وقد عاب به غيره؟ فقال: لا أدري ما يقول

rows.speaker: جنيد
rows.claim: Junayd answers by analogy: a lover's conduct, blameworthy in anyone else, is pleasing when done by the beloved, and the questioner understands.
rows.anchor: سأل رجل جنيدا كيف رضي المكر لنفسه، وقد عاب به غيره؟ فقال: لا أدري ما يقول ولكن لسيد بني [ ..... ] الطبرانية:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's allowing their plot is itself a plot against them; here He makes the would-be killer resemble Jesus, so that the man is crucified while Jesus is raised.
rows.anchor: إن تخليته إياهم مع المكر به. مكر منه بهم، ومكر الله تعالى خاص بهم في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the Israelite king's men pursued Jesus, but Gabriel lifted him through a skylight; God made a man sent to kill him look like Jesus, and they crucified that man.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إن ملك بني إسرائيل أراد قتل عيسى،

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb recounts that Jesus foretold a disciple's betrayal before the cock crow; the disciple sold him for 200 dirhams, was made to resemble Jesus and crucified, while Jesus was raised and later comforted Mary after seven days.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: طرقوا عيسى في بعض الليل فأسروه ونصبوا خشبة ليصلبوه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes human weakness to mean that humanity was created from lowly fluid, citing 30:54, which says people were created from weakness.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: هو أن خلقه من ماء مهين بيانه قول الله: الذي خلقكم من ضعف

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan says a person is weak because desire and appetite draw him in, while fear and grief unsettle him.
rows.anchor: ابن كيسان: (خلق الإنسان ضعيفا) يستميله هواه وشهوته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says eight verses in al-Nisaʾ are better for this community than all that the sun rises and sets upon: 4:26, 4:27, 4:28, 4:31, 4:48, 4:40, 4:110, and 4:147.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ثمان آيات في سورة النساء هي خير لهذه الأمة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses ترتجي in a warning about meeting defenders, as a lexical illustration in the discussion of hope and fear.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: لا ترتجي حين تلاقي الذائدا

rows.speaker: الهذلي
rows.claim: A Hudhali poet describes a honey collector who is stung by bees and does not fear another sting.
rows.anchor: وقال الهذلي: يصف [معتار] العسل ذا النوب وهي النحل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hope and fear are distinct meanings: one cannot say 'I hoped for you' intending 'I feared you,' or reverse the terms.
rows.anchor: قال: ولا يجوز رجوتك وأنت تريد خفتك ولا خفتك وأنت تريد رجوتك

words: لِتَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِمَآ أَرَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Taʿma of Banu Zafar stole Qatada ibn al-Nuʿman's armor in a leaking flour sack and hid it with Zayd ibn al-Samin. His clan urged the Prophet to defend him, and revelation condemned that plea.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس: نزلت هذه الآية في رجل من الأنصار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another version, Taʿma stole an Ansari's armor in a sack of bran; its trail led to Zayd ibn al-Samin, and the Prophet nearly ordered the Jewish man's hand cut off before the verse came down.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن ابن عباس قال: إن طعمة سرق درعا من أنصاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlabī gives three senses for prophets' seeking forgiveness: a fault before prophethood, a fault of their community or kin, or leaving a permitted act before it was prohibited.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الاستغفار في جميع الأنبياء يعد وجوه منها ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the relevant response as hearing and obeying what was commanded, avoiding what was forbidden, and being granted success in doing so.
rows.anchor: ومعناه بالسمع والطاعة لما أمرت به ونهيت عنه وحملت التوفيق عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses يستخفون as hiding and feeling ashamed before people, though they neither hide nor feel ashamed before God; God's being with them means His knowledge.
rows.anchor: يستخفون من الناس أي يستترون ويستحيون من الناس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains يبيتون as what the conspirators say at night.
rows.anchor: الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس: يعني يقولون

rows.speaker: أبو رزين
rows.claim: Abu Razin says the phrase refers to their concocting speech God does not approve, namely the claim that the Jew stole the armor.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رزين: يولعون ما لا يرضى من القول يعني بأن اليهودي سرقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlabī glosses God's encompassing their deeds as His having encompassed their good works.
rows.anchor: وكان الله بما يعملون محيطا يعني قد أحاط الله بأعمالهم الحسنة

rows.speaker: الجهمية والمعتزلة
rows.claim: The Jahmiyya and Muʿtazila infer from God's being with the plotters that He is present everywhere.
rows.anchor: وتعلقت الجهمية والمعتزلة بهذه الآية، استدلوا منها على إن الله بكل مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlabī rejects that inference: 'with them' means God knows what they say and do, whether public or hidden, and does not entail His being everywhere.
rows.anchor: وليس في وله وهو معهم ما يوجب انه بكل مكان لأنه قال أأمنتم من في السماء أن يخسف بكم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To support God's transcendence above the world, Thaʿlabī adds that good words ascend to Him and that He directs affairs from heaven to earth.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى (إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب) وقال: يدبر الأمر من السماء إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جادلتم means you disputed or pleaded for Taʿma; جدل itself is forceful twisting, as in a strongly built man and the powerful eagle.
rows.anchor: والمطلب به في اللغة بشدة [المخاصمة] وهو من الجدل وهو [شدة الفتل وفيه: رجل مجدول الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address ها أنتم هؤلاء uses ها as an attention marker meaning 'O you here.'
rows.anchor: ثم أقبل على قوم طعمة وقال ها أنتم هؤلاء أي يا هؤلاء للتنبيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies God's favor and mercy as Islam and the Qurʾan, and says a group from Thaqif tried to lead Muhammad astray.
rows.anchor: جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس، ثم قال: ولولا فضل الله. عليك ورحمته يعني به الإسلام والقرآن لهمت طائفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Thaqif delegation offered allegiance only if there were no resurrection, they could keep their idols, and they could honor al-ʿUzza for a year; Muhammad refused, and God protected him.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن وفد ثقيف قدموا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا: يا محمد قد جئناك نبايعك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The plotters harm only themselves; they cannot strip Muhammad of prophethood, since God made him worthy of it.
rows.anchor: فقال وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم يعني وفد ثقيف وما يضرونك من شيء يعني لا يستطيعون أن يزيلوا عنك النبوة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the Book and Wisdom as the rulings, and what Muhammad was taught as the religious ordinances.
rows.anchor: ثم قال وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة يعني الأحكام وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم من الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great divine favor bestowed on Muhammad is faith.
rows.anchor: وكان فضل الله أي من الله عليك بالإيمان عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two sons of Adam are Abel (Habil) and Cain (Qabil); Thaʿlabī records three forms for Habil's name and five for Qabil's.
rows.anchor: واتل عليهم نبأ خبر ابني آدم وهما هابيل وقابيل، فهابيل في اسمه ثلاث لغات

rows.speaker: أهل العلم بالقرآن
rows.claim: Scholars say Eve bore Adam twins, a boy and girl, in each pregnancy except Seth, who was born alone; she had forty children across twenty pregnancies, from Cain and Aqlima to ʿAbd al-Mughith and his twin.
rows.anchor: وكان سبب تقربهما القربان على ما ذكره أهل العلم بالقرآن. أن حواء كانت تلد لآدم (عليه السلام) توأما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Adam lived until his children and grandchildren numbered forty thousand, and saw among them adultery, wine drinking, and corruption.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يمت آدم (عليه السلام) حتى بلغ ولده وولد ولده أربعين ألفا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One account says Adam first approached Eve a hundred years after their descent, and she bore Cain and his twin before Abel and his twin in the next pregnancy.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: غشى آدم حواء بعد هبوطهما إلى الأرض بمائة سنة فولدت له قابيل وتوأمته أقليما

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الكتاب
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits from People of the Book that Cain and his twin were conceived in Paradise before the sin and born without labor or blood; after descent, Eve's pregnancy with Abel and his twin brought ordinary discomfort and blood.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: عن بعض أهل الكتاب، العلم الأول إن آدم كان يغشى حواء في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the first generation, when children matured, they married siblings from other pregnancies; a twin sister was forbidden because Eve and her daughters were the only women.
rows.anchor: وكان آدم إذا شب أولاده تزوج غلام هذا البطن جارية البطن الآخر

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Cain and Aqlima were born first, then Abel and Luwaiza two years later; Adam told Cain to marry Luwaiza and Abel to marry Aqlima, Cain's twin.
rows.anchor: في قول الكلبي. وأدركوا أمر الله عز وجل آدم (عليه السلام) أن ينكح قابيل ليوذا أخت هابيل

rows.speaker: قابيل
rows.claim: Cain refused the match, claiming his twin was more beautiful, born in Paradise, and rightfully his; Adam answered that she was forbidden and proposed that the accepted offering decide.
rows.anchor: وقال: هي أختي ولدت معي في بطن. وهي أحسن من أخت هابيل وأنا أحق بها منه

rows.speaker: معاوية بن عمار
rows.claim: Asked al-Sadiq whether Adam married his daughter to his son, Muʿawiya ibn ʿAmmar reports the answer: God forbid; Adam's religion was the same as the Prophet's, who would not accept that.
rows.anchor: وقال معاوية بن عمار: سألت الصادق عليه سلام الله عن آدم (عليه السلام) أكان زوج ابنته من ابنه، فقال: معاذ الله

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq's alternative account says Eve first bore Luwaiza, then Cain and Abel; God paired Cain with the jinni woman Jihana and Abel with the houri Nuzla, after which Cain envied his brother.
rows.anchor: فلما أدرك قابيل أظهر الله جنية من ولد الجان يقال لها جهانة في صورة إنسية

rows.speaker: آدم
rows.claim: In al-Sadiq's report, Adam tells Cain that merit belongs to God, who gives it to whom He wills, and proposes the offerings to settle who deserves precedence.
rows.anchor: فقال له آدم: يا بني إن الفضل بيد الله يؤتيه من يشاء. فقال: لا ولكنك آثرته علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say an accepted offering was consumed by fire from heaven; if rejected, no fire came and birds or beasts ate it.
rows.anchor: قالوا: وكانت القرابين إذا كانت مقبولة نزلت نار من السماء فأكلتها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain, a farmer, offered inferior grain indifferently and intended to marry his twin regardless; Abel, a shepherd, offered his finest lamb, milk, and butter sincerely.
rows.anchor: وكان قابيل صاحب زرع وقرب حبرة من طعام من أردى زرع وأضمر في نفسه: ما أبالي أيقبل مني أم لا

rows.speaker: إسماعيل بن رافع
rows.claim: Ibn Rafiʿ says Abel prized one lamb above all his wealth and offered it; fire consumed Abel's lamb, milk, and butter, but not Cain's grain, because Abel's heart was pure.
rows.anchor: وقال إسماعيل بن رافع: بلغني أن هابيل أمنح له غنمه وكان في حملتها حمل فأحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire accepted Abel's offering and rejected Cain's; the rejection exposed Cain's envy and malice.
rows.anchor: وقبل قربان هابيل لأنه كان زاكي القلب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accepted lamb continued grazing in Paradise until it became the ransom for Abraham's son.
rows.anchor: فما زال يرتع في الجنة حتى فدى به ابن إبراهيم فذلك قوله عز وجل فتقبل من أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before leaving for Mecca to visit the House, Adam asked heaven, earth, and mountains to safeguard his children; all refused, but Cain accepted, then betrayed the trust and killed Abel.
rows.anchor: فلما أراد أن يأتي مكة قال للسماء: احفظي ولدي بالأمانة فأبت، وقال ذلك للأرض فأبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlabī links Cain's bearing and betraying the trust to 33:72, which says the heavens, earth, and mountains declined it while the human being bore it, unjust and ignorant.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك قوله إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السماوات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While Adam was away, Cain threatened Abel in Gaza, resenting the accepted offering, the marriage pairing, and the public view that Abel was better; Abel replied that God accepts only from the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: قالوا: فلما غاب آدم أتى قابيل وهابيل وهو في غزة

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar swears that the murdered brother was the stronger of the two, but scruple kept him from raising his hand against his brother.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر: أيم الله إن كان المقتول لأشد الرجلين ولكن منعه التحرج أن يبسط إلى أخيه يده

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says that at that time a person threatened with murder was commanded to leave the attacker and not resist.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كتب عليهم في ذلك الوقت، إذا أراد رجل قتل رجل أن يتركه ولا يمتنع منه

words: إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوٓءَ بِإِثْمِى وَإِثْمِكَ
rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority of commentators say Abel means that Cain will bear the sin of murdering him in addition to Cain's prior sin.
rows.anchor: يعني بإثم قتلي إلى إثمك الذي عملته قبل قتلي، هذا قول عامة المفسرين.

words: إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوٓءَ بِإِثْمِى وَإِثْمِكَ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid's alternative gloss is that Cain will bear both Abel's wrongdoing and the blood guilt, showing they were already morally accountable and subject to promise and threat.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال: معناه إني أريد أن يكون عليك خطيئتي التي عملتها أنا إذا قتلتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that Cain's soul complied with him and made a pact with him to kill his brother.
rows.anchor: فطوعت له نفسه أي طاوعته وبايعته في قتل أخيه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as 'emboldened him.'
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: شجعت. قتادة: زينت. فقتله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah glosses the phrase as 'adorned it for him.'
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: شجعت. قتادة: زينت. فقتله

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Cain evaded Abel in the mountains, then found him asleep while tending sheep and smashed his head with a rock.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: فلما أراد قتل هابيل راغ الغلام في رؤوس الجبال.

rows.speaker: ابن جريح
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Cain did not know how to kill; Iblis demonstrated by crushing a bird's head between stones, and Cain copied him. Abel was twenty; accounts differ about where he died.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريح: لم يدر قابيل كيف يقتل هابيل، فتمثل له إبليس وأخذ طيرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas locates Abel's killing on Mount Nawd.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: على جبل نود، وقال بعضهم: عند عقبة حرا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another account places the killing near the pass of Hira.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: على جبل نود، وقال بعضهم: عند عقبة حرا

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq locates the killing at the site of the Great Mosque in Basra.
rows.anchor: حكى محمد بن جرير، وقال جعفر الصادق: بالبصرة في موضع المسجد الأعظم

words: فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَابًۭا يَبْحَثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain did not know how to dispose of the first human corpse; he carried Abel in a sack for a year as beasts and birds waited, until God sent two fighting crows and the survivor buried the other.
rows.anchor: فلما قتله بالعراء لم يدر ما يصنع به، لأنه كان أول ميت على وجه الأرض من بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here سوءة أخي means the brother's corpse; the story also proves that the whole dead body is a person's ʿawra.
rows.anchor: فأواري سوأة أخي أي جيفته وفيه دليل على أن الميت كله عورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlabī says Cain regretted carrying the corpse, not killing Abel; another view says he regretted his brother's death, not committing the sin.
rows.anchor: فأصبح من النادمين على حمله لا على قتله، وقيل: على موت أخيه لا على ركوب الذنب

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Awzaʿi reports from al-Muttalib ibn ʿAbd Allah that the earth shook for seven days after Abel's murder, drank his blood, and was forbidden ever to drink blood again; God confronted Cain over the blood crying from the ground.
rows.anchor: يدل عليه ما أخبر الأوزاعي عن المطلب بن عبد الله المخزومي قال: لما قتل ابن آدم أخاه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says that while Adam was in Mecca, Cain's murder made trees uproot, foods change, fruit sour, water bitter, and the earth dusty; Adam sensed an event and found Abel dead in India.
rows.anchor: مقاتل بن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: لما قتل قابيل هابيل وآدم بمكة اشتال الشجر

rows.speaker: آدم
rows.claim: The account attributes to Adam an elegy for Abel, beginning with the changed land and its dust-covered face.
rows.anchor: فأنشأ يقول، وهو أول من قال الشعر: تغيرت البلاد ومن عليها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, as transmitted by Maymun ibn Mihran, rejects the claim that Adam composed Arabic poetry, saying it falsely accuses Adam and citing 36:69 that Muhammad was not taught poetry.
rows.anchor: وروى ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس قال: من قال إن آدم قال شعرا فقد كذب على الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reconciles the elegy by saying Adam lamented in Syriac, not Arabic poetry; he entrusted it to Seth, and it passed to Yaʿrub ibn Qahtan, who reordered it into meter without adding or removing a letter and was the first to write Arabic.
rows.anchor: إن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم والأنبياء كلهم صلوات الله عليهم في النهي عن الشعر سواء، قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continued elegy mourns Abel's death, the burial that holds him, and Adam's grief and weariness with life after losing his son.
rows.anchor: ل فوا حزني لقد فقد المليح

rows.speaker: إبليس
rows.claim: Iblis answers Adam's lament with a taunting poem, telling him to leave the land and blaming his loss of Paradise on Iblis's schemes.
rows.anchor: فأجابه إبليس في جوف الليل شامتا: تنح عن البلاد وساكنيها

rows.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
rows.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd says Adam mourned for a hundred years; at age 130, five years after Abel's murder, Eve bore Seth, whose name means God's gift and who replaced Abel.
rows.anchor: وقال سالم بن أبي الجعد: لما قتل هابيل مكث آدم (عليه السلام) مائة سنة لا أكثر

rows.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
rows.claim: In the same account, God taught Seth the hours of night and day and the worship performed in each, and made him Adam's successor.
rows.anchor: وقال سالم بن أبي الجعد: لما قتل هابيل مكث آدم (عليه السلام) مائة سنة لا أكثر. ثم أتى فقيل: حياك الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain was ordered to go as a fugitive and wanderer, afraid and shunned; he took his sister Hibatu Allah to Aden in Yemen.
rows.anchor: وأما قابيل فقيل له: اذهب طريدا شريدا فزعا مرهوبا لا يأمن من يراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis deceived Cain into thinking fire had consumed Abel's offering because Abel worshipped fire; Cain then established fire worship for his descendants, becoming the first to do so.
rows.anchor: فأتاه إبليس، فقال له: إنما أكلت النار قربان هابيل لأنه كان يعبد النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final report says Cain threw stones at passersby; a blind grandson accidentally killed Cain with a stone, then his son accused him, and the blind man killed that son with a slap.
rows.anchor: قالوا: كان لا يمر به أحدا من ولده إلا رماه، فأقبل ابن لقابيل أعمى ومعه ابن له
